questions.prompt: A click handler calls setCount(count + 1) twice in a row. What is count after one click, starting from 0?
questions.explanation: Both calls read the same render's value of count, so each queues 'set to 1'. Use the functional form setCount(c => c + 1) to increment twice.

options: Only after the first render (and its cleanup on unmount)
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array means the effect has no reactive inputs, so it runs once after mount.

questions.prompt: Why should list items rendered with map() have a stable key?
options: It makes the list render faster in all cases
React uses it to match items between renders and preserve their state
It is required by the HTML specification
It becomes the element's id attribute
questions.explanation: Keys let React identify which item is which when the list changes order or length.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a controlled input is true?
options: Its value lives in the DOM only
Its value comes from React state and changes through an onChange handler
questions.explanation: A controlled input renders value from state and updates state in onChange.

questions.prompt: A parent component re-renders on every keystroke in a search box, and a large child list below it feels slow. How would you diagnose the problem and what would you change?

rubric.criterion: Uses React DevTools Profiler (or similar) to confirm which components re-render
Moves search state down or isolates it so the list does not re-render
Mentions React.memo / useMemo / useCallback or virtualization for long lists

questions.model_answer: Profile first to see which components re-render and why. Then keep the search input state local to the search box (or debounce it) so the list is not a child of the changing state, wrap the list in React.memo with stable props, and virtualize it if it is very long.
questions.answer_text: I would open the React DevTools Profiler and record a few keystrokes to see which components re-render. Then I would move the search state into its own component so typing does not re-render the list, and wrap the list in React.memo.
questions.feedback: Clear, practical plan: profiling first and isolating the state were both on target. You could also mention virtualization for very long lists.
